label: PF Backlog 461
title: Restrict the worker/assignment path to product_forge scope (project changes use PF pipeline)
body:
Source: user scope decision (2026-10-07) captured on BI-PF-0418.

The worker/assignment path executes Product Forge's OWN backlog only. Restrict it to `product_forge` scope and
fail-closed for `project`:
- `GET /engineering/schedule/next?stage=execute` + the assignment API (`/assignments/*`) reject `scope=project`
  with a clear error (project changes go through PF's pipeline/agents).
- `job_manager.claim_next` used for external workers claims `product_forge` only (keep the per-item mechanism).
- Docs: state the two planes (product-building pipeline vs PF-backlog workers).

dashboard_impact: no UI surface.

## Divergence recorded at implementation (Reconciliation rule)
The approved assumption was "keep claim_next usable only for product_forge". Implemented at the **API boundary**
instead of the core, because guarding the core `job_manager.claim_next` broke the `lease` gate (which uses a
scratch *project* scope to exercise the mechanism). The worker boundary (coordinator/worker API) is fail-closed
via `_worker_scope` on `/assignments/*` + `stage=execute` on `/schedule/next`; the core stays the
scope-parameterized mechanism. No silent divergence - recorded here.

delivery.note: merged --no-ff; fast precheck PASS (17 gates) - small boundary change. /assignments/* use _worker_scope (product_forge-only, project rejected); /schedule/next?stage=execute rejects project; core claim_next left scope-parameterized (boundary is the right place; see divergence note).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/adopt_project.py, core/cross_project_learning.py, core/paths.py, core/pipeline_capabilities.py

_note: worker/assignment path restricted to product_forge scope
